arxiv-1908-09834.title: Probing the freeze-in mechanism in dark matter models with U ​ ( 1 ) ′ U(1)^{\prime} gauge extensions
arxiv-1908-09834.creator: Saniya Heeba, Felix Kahlhoefer
arxiv-1908-09834.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Saniya Heeba, Felix Kahlhoefer. New gauge bosons at the MeV scale with tiny gauge couplings (so-called dark photons) can be responsible for the freeze-in production of dark matter and provide a clear target for present and future experiments. We study the effects of thermal mixing between dark photons and Standard Model gauge bosons and of the resulting plasmon decays on dark matter production before and after the electroweak phase transition.

arxiv-2203-02913.title: Delorme’s intertwining conditions for sections of homogeneous vector bundles on two and three dimensional hyperbolic spaces
arxiv-2203-02913.creator: Martin Olbrich, Guendalina Palmirotta
arxiv-2203-02913.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Martin Olbrich, Guendalina Palmirotta. The description of the Paley-Wiener space for compactly supported smooth functions C c ∞ ​ ( G ) C^{\infty}_{c}(G) on a semi-simple Lie group G G involves certain intertwining conditions that are difficult to handle. In the present paper, we make them completely explicit for G = 𝐒𝐋 ​ ( 2 , ℝ ) d G=\mathbf{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})^{d} ( d ∈ ℕ d\in\mathbb{N} ) and G = 𝐒𝐋 ⁡ ( 2 , ℂ ) G=\mathbf{SL}(2,\mathbb{C}) .

arxiv-2204-11330.title: Quantum chaos and Hénon-Heiles model: Dirac’s variational approach with Jackiw-Kerman function
arxiv-2204-11330.creator: Choon-Lin Ho, Chung-I Chou
arxiv-2204-11330.description: Abstract A simple semiclassical Hénon-Heiles model is constructed based on Dirac’s time-dependent variational principle. We obtain an effective semiclassical Hamiltonian using a Hartree-type two-body trial wavefunction in the Jackiw-Kerman form. Numerical results show that quantum effects can in fact induce chaos in the non-chaotic regions of the classical Hénon-Heiles model.

arxiv-2205-00508.title: The Best of Both Worlds: Combining Model-based and Nonparametric Approaches for 3D Human Body Estimation
arxiv-2205-00508.creator: Zhe Wang, Jimei Yang, Charless Fowlkes
arxiv-2205-00508.description: Abstract Nonparametric based methods have recently shown promising results in reconstructing human bodies from monocular images while model-based methods can help correct these estimates and improve prediction. However, estimating model parameters from global image features may lead to noticeable misalignment between the estimated meshes and image evidence.

arxiv-2206-12526.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ambroise Grau. Sets and vector spaces being particular examples of independence algebras, a natural question that arises is whether by taking the semigroup T ⁡ ( 𝒜 , ℬ ) T(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}) of all endomorphisms of an independence algebra 𝒜 \mathcal{A} whose image lie in a subalgebra ℬ \mathcal{B} , one can obtain corresponding

arxiv-2209-14703.title: Fully Lattice Linear Algorithms Thanks: Extended version of the paper with the same title to appear in The 24th International Symposium on Stabilization, Safety, and Security of Distributed Systems (SSS 2022).
arxiv-2209-14703.creator: Arya Tanmay Gupta, Sandeep S Kulkarni
arxiv-2209-14703.description: Abstract This paper focuses on analyzing and differentiating between lattice linear problems and algorithms. It introduces a new class of algorithms called (fully) lattice linear algorithms . A property of these algorithms is that they induce a partial order among all states and form multiple lattices . An initial state locks in one of these lattices.

arxiv-2303-17312.title: New techniques for jet calibration with the ATLAS detector
arxiv-2303-17312.description: Abstract A determination of the jet energy scale is presented using proton–proton collision data with a centre-of-mass energy of s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 140 fb -1 collected using the ATLAS detector at the LHC.

arxiv-2305-12911.creator: Kwassi Anani
arxiv-2305-12911.description: Abstract This paper aims at obtaining, by means of integral transforms, analytical approximations in short times of solutions to boundary value problems for the one-dimensional reaction-diffusion equation with constant coefficients. The general form of the equation is considered on a bounded generic interval and the three classical types of boundary conditions, i.e.

arxiv-2404-16900.title: Space-Variant Total Variation boosted by learning techniques in few-view tomographic imaging
arxiv-2404-16900.creator: Elena Morotti, Davide Evangelista, Andrea Sebastiani, Elena Loli Piccolomini
arxiv-2404-16900.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Elena Morotti, Davide Evangelista, Andrea Sebastiani, Elena Loli Piccolomini. This paper focuses on the development of a space-variant regularization model for solving an under-determined linear inverse problem. The case study is a medical image reconstruction from few-view tomographic noisy data. The primary objective of the proposed optimization model is to achieve a good balance between denoising and the preservation of fine details and edges, overcoming the performance of the popular and largely used Total Variation (TV) regularization through the application of appropriate pixel-dependent weights.

arxiv-2406-18823.title: Emergence of metachronal waves in a chain of symmetrically beating filaments
arxiv-2406-18823.creator: Narina Jung, Won Kyu Kim, Changbong Hyeon
arxiv-2406-18823.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Narina Jung, Won Kyu Kim, Changbong Hyeon. Recent experiments have shown that metachronal waves (MCWs) can emerge from a chain of symmetrically beating nematodes aligned at the edge of sessile droplets. Our study, employing a coupled elastohydrodynamic model of active filaments, elucidates that a misalignment caused by a tilt against the bounding wall disrupts the synchronization and generates a constant time lag between adjacent filaments, giving rise to MCWs.

arxiv-2502-14369.title: Feedback-Based Quantum Strategies for Constrained Combinatorial Optimization Problems
arxiv-2502-14369.creator: Salahuddin Abdul Rahman, Özkan Karabacak, Rafal Wisniewski
arxiv-2502-14369.description: Abstract Feedback-based quantum algorithms have recently emerged as potential methods for approximating the ground states of Hamiltonians. One such algorithm, the feedback-based algorithm for quantum optimization (FALQON), is specifically designed to solve quadratic unconstrained binary optimization problems. Its extension, the feedback-based algorithm for quantum optimization with constraints (FALQON-C), was introduced to handle constrained optimization problems with equality and inequality constraints.

arxiv-2504-21521.title: Adaptive Neural Control with Desired Approximation: An Integral Lyapunov Function Approach
arxiv-2504-21521.creator: Mingxuan Sun, Shengxiang Zou
arxiv-2504-21521.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mingxuan Sun, Shengxiang Zou. The inherent approximation ability of neural networks plays an essential role in adaptive neural control, where the prerequisite for existence of the compact set is crucial in the control designs. Instead of using practical system state, in this paper, the desired approximation approach is characterized to tackle such a problem, where the desired state signal is required only as the input to the network.

pmc-10575412.title: Drug Loaded 3D-Printed Poly(ε-Caprolactone) Scaffolds for Local Antibacterial or Anti-Inflammatory Treatment in Bone Regeneration
pmc-10575412.creator: Mariia Stepanova, Ilia Averianov, Iosif Gofman, Natalia Shevchenko, Artem Rubinstein, Tatiana Egorova, Andrey Trulioff, Yulia Nashchekina, Igor Kudryavtsev, Elena Demyanova, Evgenia Korzhikova-Vlakh, Viktor Korzhikov-Vlakh, Annalisa Chiappone
pmc-10575412.description: Annual bone grafting surgeries due to bone fractures, resections of affected bones, skeletal anomalies, osteoporosis, etc. exceed two million worldwide. In this regard, the creation of new materials for bone tissue repair is one of the urgent tasks of modern medicine. Additive manufacturing, or 3D printing, offers great opportunities for the development of materials with diverse properties and designs.

pmc-11480098.title: Decoding sex-specific metabolomic biomarkers in the loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta)
pmc-11480098.creator: P. J. Marín-García, D. García-Párraga, J. L. Crespo-Picazo, N. I. Stacy, L. Llobat, M. Cambra-López, E. Blas, J. J. Pascual, T. Larsen, M. S. Hedemann
pmc-11480098.description: There is need for advancing minimally invasive diagnostic techniques for sex differentiation at early life-stage classes in sea turtles. The objectives of this study were to determine whether there are sex-specific effects on the metabolome of the loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta) and to identify potential biomarkers for sex classification at early life-stage classes (50 post-hatchling and 50 juvenile).

pmc-11510562.title: Distinct Solubilization Mechanisms of Medroxyprogesterone in Gemini Surfactant Micelles: A Comparative Study with Progesterone
pmc-11510562.creator: Hiromichi Nakahara, Kazutaka Koga, Keisuke Matsuoka
pmc-11510562.description: The solubilization behavior of medroxyprogesterone (MP) within gemini surfactant micelles (14-6-14,2Br−) was investigated and compared with that of progesterone to uncover distinct solubilization mechanisms. We employed 1H-NMR and 2D ROESY spectroscopy to elucidate the spatial positioning of MP within the micelle, revealing that MP integrates more deeply into the micellar core.

pmc-11526422.title: Unraveling Interdiffusion Phenomena and the Role of Nanoscale Diffusion Barriers in the Copper–Gold System
pmc-11526422.creator: Lilian M Vogl, Peter Schweizer, Xavier Maeder, Ivo Utke, Andrew M Minor, Johann Michler
pmc-11526422.description: Diffusion is one of the most fundamental concepts in materials science, playing a pivotal role in materials synthesis, forming, and degradation. Of particular importance is solid state interdiffusion of metals which defines the usable parameter space for material combinations in the form of alloys. This parameter space can be explored on the macroscopic scale by using diffusion couples.

pmc-12551232.creator: Sarah Piper, Victoria Loblay, Yun Ju Christine Song, Grace Yeeun Lee, Samantha Huntley, Olivia Iannelli, Nicholas Ho, Seyed Hossein Hosseini, Catherine Vacher, Alexis Hutcheon, Paul Crosland, Kristen Tran, Kim-Huong Nguyen, Chloe Gosling, Jordan van Rosmalen, Kayla Andrade, Ian B. Hickie, Jo-An Occh
pmc-12551232.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAustralia’s mental health system needs to expand rapidly to meet the growing demand for care by young Australians. Participatory systems modelling (PSM) has emerged as a valuable method for guiding strategic decision-making in mental health policy.MethodsThis paper evaluates the participatory methods and approaches utilised in a series of PSM workshops focused on the development of a youth mental health decision-support tool for the Brisbane South region, Queensland.

pmc-13335875.title: Phase‐Resolved Defect Transport Mechanisms Governing Asynchronous Ordering in a Eutectic High‐Entropy Alloy
pmc-13335875.creator: Huiwen Yao, Qingshuang Ma, Jie Xiong, Jing Bai, Huijun Li, Qiuzhi Gao
pmc-13335875.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Eutectic high‐entropy alloys (EHEAs) exhibit asynchronous phase evolution under identical thermal conditions, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we investigated the isothermal annealing of AlCoCrCuFeNi alloy using phase‐resolved experiments and atomistic simulations. Electron microscopy revealed sharply contrasting structural pathways: the initially disordered BCC‐FeCr phase progressively developed long‐range order, whereas the B2‐NiAl phase retained its macroscopically ordered framework while undergoing local structural relaxation. Molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations traced this discrepancy to phase‐dependent defect energetics.

pmc-13378348.title: The technical utilization solutions for curtailment during China’s rapid expansion of wind and PV power
pmc-13378348.creator: Libo Zhang, Huan Zhang, Haobo Ren, Pengcheng Tang, Qunwei Wang, Dequn Zhou
pmc-13378348.description: SummaryWith the continued rapid growth of installed capacity for wind and PV power in China, the challenge of wind and PV power curtailment has become increasingly pressing. This study quantifies the spatiotemporal distributions and evolving trends of wind and PV curtailment for 31 provinces in China.

pmc-13475805.title: Assessing CT-based volumetric analysis via deep learning for idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus
pmc-13475805.creator: Meera Srikrishna, Woosung Seo, Anna Zettergren, Silke Kern, Daniel Cantré, Florian Gessler, Houman Sotoudeh, Jakob Seidlitz, Joshua D Bernstock, Lars-Olof Wahlund, Eric Westman, Ingmar Skoog, Johan Virhammar, David Fällmar, Michael Schöll
pmc-13475805.description: Brain computed tomography (CT) is an accessible and commonly utilized technique for assessing brain structure. In cases of idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH), the presence of ventriculomegaly is often neuroradiologically evaluated by visual rating and manual measurement of each image. Previously, we have developed a deep-learning-model that utilizes transfer learning from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for CT-based intracranial tissue segmentation.

pmc-13531738.creator: Jiayi Ren, Qiuyu Yang, Haoxiang He, Jin Li, Hang Gao, Chen Yang, Yan Cao, Yuting Wen, Chen Chen, Marim Kandil, Jiming Tao

pmc-13572700.title: Occupational exposures and worker health in decarbonization of energy-intensive industries: a scoping review protocol
pmc-13572700.creator: Johanna Samulin Erdem, Ingrid Løken Jørgensen, Lina Wik
pmc-13572700.description: Energy-intensive industries account for a substantial share of the global greenhouse gas emissions. The transition to net-zero emissions by 2050 demands development of industrial infrastructure and implementation of low-carbon technologies. This transition is expected to result in altered exposure scenarios for workers.

pmc-13638336.title: Health, poverty and employment effects of cutting income replacement benefits for the disabled: a difference-in-differences analysis of the 2017 welfare reforms
pmc-13638336.creator: Huihui Song, Roberta Piroddi, Philip McHale, Benjamin Barr
pmc-13638336.description: BackgroundHealth-related economic inactivity in England has risen, with more working-age adults claiming disability and incapacity benefits. The 2016 Welfare Reform and Work Act reduced weekly payments for Employment and Support Allowance recipients deemed capable of some work from April 2017, potentially affecting poverty, mental health and employment among people with long-term conditions (LTCs). Evidence on its causal impact is limited.

pmc-13679920.title: Failure of Implantable Cardioverter-defibrillator Pacing Capture in BRASH Syndrome with Severe Hyperkalemia
pmc-13679920.creator: Stephen Roche, Michael Kanan, Deana Mikhalkova
pmc-13679920.description: This case report describes a 54-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease and heart failure who presented with BRASH syndrome: a synergistic cycle of bradycardia, renal failure, atrioventricular nodal blockade, shock, and hyperkalemia. The patient, who was adherent to metoprolol and amiodarone, presented with a profound ventricular escape rhythm of 16 bpm and hemodynamic instability after missing 4 days of hemodialysis.
